To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
people's beliefs and illusions about their learning are not only inaccurate but also often self-fulfilling.
people's beliefs about how learning occurs are often incorrect, and that their ongoing assessments of learning are often influenced by current performance.

learners need to believe that learning can be self-regulated and that they have the ability to self-regulate their learning, and to know that learning is an active process that is affected by their own efforts, that learning can occur without effort, and that effortful learning can lead to overconfidence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question, "Why are people not better at learning?"
how people learn and how people think they learn.
how learners think about their learning, how they regulate their own learning, and the illusions that can undermine their effectiveness.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the research on self-regulated learning has been quite successful in identifying the beliefs, techniques, and illusions that can lead to effective learning and in identifying those that lead to poor learning.
self-regulated learning has become increasingly more important in recent years and that the need to understand the processes of self-regulated learning is more important than ever before.

self-regulated learning is a complex and multifaceted phenomenon that is still poorly understood, and that the current state of the field is one of a great deal of activity but relatively little progress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more we understand about how people learn, the less they know about how they learn.
people often have faulty beliefs about how they learn, and that this can have important implications for how well they manage their own learning.
the more people know about how they learn, the better off they will be in terms of learning and remembering, and that this knowledge can help them become better self-regulated learners.
The main takeaway from our work is that

learners need to understand the distinction between the subjective experience of learning and objective measures of learning, and to understand that the subjective sense of learning and remembering is often an imperfect guide to the objective reality of learning and remembering.

learners need to understand the importance of their own beliefs and assessments, and the role that they play in determining their learning, if they are to become maximally effective in their learning.
people need to be taught how to learn, and that they need to learn how to learn in ways that are compatible with the way the mind actually works.
